slots.title: Trump plans federal “AI Force” and AI czar
slots.body:
Trump said Saturday he is creating an “AI Force” for federal oversight of artificial intelligence and will announce an AI “czar” in the near future.

Reuters and WSJ reported the move the same day, alongside stories about industry alarm and voter pushback on AI.

Sky News tied the announcement to a lawsuit claiming companies illegally agreed to slow AI development.

No major U.S. equity index level in the feed is tied to this headline alone; the prior session had the S&P 500 at 7,650.50, up 0.2%.

What part of AI policy do you think gets the most airtime next — safety, competition, or federal structure?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 19, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished +0.2% at 7,650.50, up 12.74 points from a prior close of 7,637.76, with an intraday range of 7,610.52 to 7,657.17.

The Nasdaq Composite outpaced the other U.S. benchmarks at +0.4%, closing at 26,522.54 after a 104.25-point gain; the session low was 26,333.98 and the high 26,544.93.

The CBOE Volatility Index ($VIX) fell −4.1% to 14.81, down from a prior close of 15.44, with an intraday low of 14.80.

Large semiconductor and hardware names closed higher:

$BABA stood out among ADR-sized moves at +4.3% to 113.26; $GOOGL was +0.6% to 349.54 and $GOOG +0.2% to 344.41.

Energy equities softened with oil benchmarks lower: $CVX −1.0% to 209.51 and $XOM −0.1% to 163.18 alongside Brent (BZUSD) −0.9% at 103.87 and $USO −1.0% at 153.82; gold futures (GCUSD) were +0.6% at 4,424.90.

The latest U.S. Treasury snapshot in the data (dated 2026-09-17) showed a 10-year yield of 4.9% and a 2s10s spread of 0.27 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included the Nikkei 225 at +1.4% (65,018.95), the FTSE 100 at −0.3% (10,659.13), the Hang Seng at +0.1% (24,750.78), and the iShares MSCI Germany ETF ($EWG), labeled DAX proxy, at −1.3% (42.15).
